meta.contract: This file is the public contract. Build on it rather than on the project's internals: it is versioned with each deploy, contains no student data by construction, and reproduces no item text.
meta.itemText: Where `transcribed` is true, the stem, answer choices and figures are a reviewed transcription of the official released item, not an automatic extraction: the prose comes from the PDF's own text layer character for character and only the mathematics is filled in, from vector glyph geometry. Where `transcribed` is false there is no question text at all -- use sourceUrl, which points at the exact page. Every item links to the official PDF either way.
meta.pValueCaveat: pValue is NYSED's own published statewide figure. For a constructed-response item it is average points earned divided by total possible points, so it is not the same quantity as a multiple-choice percent-correct -- do not put them on one axis. NYSED does not publish the population it is computed over.
meta.releaseCaveat: Never publish a '% of the test released' figure. NYSED's promise is 'at least 75 percent of the test questions that counted toward students' scores' -- the denominator is SCORED items, and designedItems above includes embedded field-test items that do not count and whose number NYSED does not publish. Dividing released items by designedItems gives 63-65% for 2023-2025, which looks like NYSED breaking its own promise and is simply the wrong denominator. Report released item counts, never a share of the test.

keySources.g7-2026: The key is NYSED's own, read from the Map to the Standards on page 38 of the released-items PDF -- which is a materially different situation from RegentsAlign, where the key lives in a separate scoring-key document and had to be derived independently first. Here the item map IS the official publication, and it is the same table this project's item data comes from. Three things guard it. First, tools/preflight.py re-derives every multiple-choice key by a second, unrelated code path -- a naive plain-reading-order re-read of the PDF with no geometry at all -- and compares; across the twelve tests that is 282 keys with no disagreement. Second, the NYCPS 'NYS Exam IM Alignment' sheets in sources/nycps/ independently agree with our standard for 256 of 273 items on the 2023-2025 tests, and where they differ ours is the more precise reading. Third, several items were checked arithmetically against the decoded content rather than taken on trust: item 15's choices decode to -8/15, -3/40, 3/40, 8/15 and -1/5 x 3/8 = -3/40, which is choice B and matches the published key; item 21's choices differ only by their inequality symbol and decode to 20x+5<=200, 20x+5<200, 5x+20>=200, 5x+20>200, of which 5x+20>=200 is the artist earning at least $200, which is choice C and matches. NOT claimed: that all 34 answers were solved from scratch before the key was consulted.
keySources.g8-2026: The key is NYSED's own, read from the Map to the Standards in the released-items PDF and carried into provenance/itemmap_g8-2026.json by tools/extract_item_map.py. tools/merge_content.py re-checks every letter against that file item by item and refuses to build if one disagrees, so the key in this spec cannot drift from the official table or be shifted by one released item. It was additionally checked against the transcribed choices: nine of the 34 are decided by reading the mathematics rather than the prose -- item 7's Pythagorean equation, item 15's product of powers, item 3's quotient of powers -- and in every case the keyed letter is the one the transcription makes true.
keySources.g6-2026: The key is NYSED's own, read from the Map to the Standards in the released-items PDF and carried into provenance/itemmap_g6-2026.json by tools/extract_item_map.py. tools/merge_content.py re-checks every letter against that file item by item and refuses to build if one disagrees. It was additionally checked against the transcribed content: item 8's key is P, and P is the point at negative four and a half on this item's own number line, which is the opposite of the four and a half in its stem; item 10's key is 27, and the three points in its graph -- 2 minutes at 18 gallons, 4 at 36, 6 at 54 -- give 9 gallons a minute, so 3 minutes is 27; item 20's key is the only choice whose two comparisons are both true of the transcribed absolute values.
keySources.g8-2023: The key is NYSED's own, read from the Map to the Standards in the released-items PDF and carried into provenance/itemmap_g8-2023.json by tools/extract_item_map.py. tools/merge_content.py re-checks every letter against that file item by item and refuses to build if one disagrees, so the key here cannot drift from the official table or be shifted by one released item. Every constructed-response answer below cites NYSED's own exemplary-response page and is checked against this project's transcription of the same item, so the two corroborate each other.

g7-2026: Item 27's missing y -- 'the amount of juice, , that can be made' -- and the same gap in item 7's 'a proportional relationship between  and x' are both CLOSED. The cause was that where maths is lifted out of a sentence the PDF's text layer leaves a space, and that space's box is as wide as the value that is missing, so the reader treated it as occupied and hid the very glyph belonging there. Whitespace no longer occupies a line.
Item 7's repeating-decimal overbar covers '.3' rather than just the '3', so 3.3-repeating renders with the bar one character too wide.

Item 47 is a displayed expression published as an image rather than as text. It reads correctly; it is simply less good than markup would be. Item 20 was in the same state until wide fraction bars were admitted to the glyph table, and now renders as text.
Item 31's displayed expression decodes as '(5.2 - 1.6) + (---) = 0', where the three rules are an answer box rather than minus signs.

Two of the 42 stems carry a trailing artifact from their answer line, which in these two items shares a prose line with the end of the question: item 40 ends '...should Mr. Morgano receive? $' and item 45 ends '...in the sixth grade? Answerstudents'. Left visible rather than hand-patched, because editing a stem would break the prose-fidelity check that makes this data trustworthy -- the fix belongs in the extractor's line classification.

Three values in this test were WRONG in the first published version and are corrected here: item 34's stem read -45 over 9 where the page says -45 over -9, item 43's price list read $1 and $1 where the page says $12.50 and $10.25, and item 36's expression read x - with the 0.25x shown separately beside it. All three had the same cause -- the right-hand bound on a prose line's maths cut a value in half, and the remainder was published as a stray expression. The extractor now grows an accepted run rightwards, so a value that continues past the text is completed. Nothing was hand-edited; re-running the extractor produces these stems.

hazards: Grades 7 and 8 SWAP Units 7 and 8 between the New York and national editions. Grade 7's Unit 7 is Probability and Sampling and its Unit 8 is Angles, Triangles, and Prisms; nationally they are reversed. Grade 6 is not swapped.
The NYCPS workbooks use national numbering on their NGMLS Readiness sheet and New York numbering on sibling sheets in the same file.

Grade 8's own guide contradicts itself on Unit 6: Standards by Lesson lists 11 lessons while the Scope and Sequence box, the language table and the pacing guide all stop at 9, because NY-8.SP.4 (categorical data) was removed under NGMLS and that table was not regenerated.

The guide's two alignment tables are not exact inverses. Standards by Lesson and Lessons by Standard disagree on six pairs in grade 7, all in or beside Unit 7; NY-7.NS.2d is placed at Unit 7 Lesson 16 by one and Unit 8 Lesson 16 by the other. Both readings are kept, in tableDisagreements.

Cluster citations ('NY-7.EE.Cluster-1') are the guide's own literal form and live in clusterToLessons / lessonToClusters, never mixed in with standards. Their numbers are Imagine Learning's and are NOT resolvable to NYSED's cluster order: NY-6.SP.Cluster-5 is cited by the grade 7 guide although the grade 6 guide's own SP clusters stop at 2.
Resolve a lesson BY TITLE, never by number. This is the rule RegentsAlign lost a week to.

Match titles CASE-INSENSITIVELY. The grade 6 guide prints its Unit 9 as 'Putting it All Together' in the Scope and Sequence box and 'Putting It All Together' in the pacing table, so an exact-string title match fails against the guide's own other table. Grades 7 and 8 use only the capitalised form.

pacingConventions.days: [minimum, maximum]. Equal when the guide prints a single number. The range includes two assessment days per unit; the upper bound includes the optional lessons.
pacingConventions.midUnitAssessment: The guide's (MA) mark -- 'Unit has Mid-Unit Assessment'.
pacingConventions.optionalLessons: Lesson numbers within the unit, or [] for the guide's 'none', or the string 'all' for Unit 9, which is optional in its entirety.
pacingConventions.startWeek: 1-35, derived from the unit block's vertical position against the 35 week labels in the table's left margin. The guide does not print a start week per unit, so this is read off the layout, not quoted.
pacingConventions.dayCountFormula: The guide's own footnote: number of days for each course = Lessons + Assessments - Optional Lessons.
